text:
josh: Heads-up — in the last 2h we've seen a sustained write IOPS spike across the local-ssd (scratch) pool in gpu-prod-us-west-2. Several nodes reporting blk errors and devices going read-only.

sre-bot: Alert: disk_io_saturation detected on cluster gpu-prod-us-west-2 (severity: P2). 14 hosts > 180k write IOPS in a 5m window.

anya: Which pool exactly? dedicated GPUs or ephemeral scratch?

josh: scratch-pool-2 (worker-gpu-*). Not the reserved workloads. The background "disk-sweeper" churn that clears model cache after evictions kicked off ~03:10 UTC and coincided with the spike.

maria: Can you paste a short iostat/dmesg snippet from one affected host?

josh: ```
# iostat -x 1 3
Device            r/s     w/s    rkB/s   wkB/s  await r_await w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1         1200  250000   15000  250000   5.4    0.8    5.8    0.20  99.8

[ dmesg tail ]
blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456789
nvme nvme0: Completed cmd 0x25b5 with NVMe status: Media Error
```

maria: That looks like write amplification + firmware media_error. Could be wear-leveling / hotspots on the drive — not just OS-level queueing.

devops-lead: Immediate mitigation: throttle the cleaner. Reduce from burst mode to 10MB/s per node and add jitter/stagger windows so not all nodes clean simultaneously. Also set cleaner to prefer file-by-file deletes instead of aggressive TRIM in parallel.

david: Agreed. We should also identify worst offenders and mark devices for replacement. Josh, can you list the host IDs so I can open RMA tickets?

josh: affected hosts: worker-gpu-142, -147, -151, -203, -210, -211, -215. I'll attach full host logs to the ticket.

anya: I can push a patch to disk-sweeper to add a token-bucket limiter + randomized start delay. I'll canary to 10 nodes first.

maria: Also enable SMART attribute polling every 5m for the scratch pool and add an early "media_error" alert to the dashboard. If firmware reports remapped sectors > threshold, escalate.

devops-lead: :thumbsup: Do the canary, open RMAs, and schedule out-of-band replacements. Also temporarily disable large-scale evictions during the cleanup window (avoid cascades).

sre-bot: Incident updated: mitigation applied — cleaner throttled to 10MB/s, 10-node canary started. Monitoring metrics: write_iops, device_errors, remapped_sectors.

josh: :eyes: Canary results after 20m: IOPS down ~70% on canary nodes, device errors stopped on those 10.

david: I'll coord replacements tomorrow with HW ops and add a short postmortem/lessons learned doc. Reminder: add a pre-clean safety check to prevent overlapped cleans on dense racks.

maria: Good call. After replacements, run a full scrub and resume normal alerts.

josh: Thanks everyone — keeping this thread open till RMAs are scheduled and the canary is green.
